subject.title: Telegram voice message delayed ~15 minutes before agent dispatch, then run aborts

question: Should this combined Telegram voice report remain open as the umbrella for voice dispatch latency plus aborted/no-reply fallback, or should maintainers split the remaining work under narrower Telegram voice-recovery and fallback issues now that the ingress-drain fix has shipped?
rationale: Current main partially fixes the delayed ingress class, but the remaining visible fallback behavior is user-facing policy and cannot be safely changed by cleanup automation without choosing the intended Telegram direct-message semantics.

options.title: Keep As Umbrella Until Live Repro
options.body: Keep this issue open until a live Telegram repro or maintainer trace confirms the exact remaining voice abort/fallback boundary, then split only after the root cause is known.

options.title: Split Remaining Work To Voice Recovery
options.body: Move the generated-reply delivery portion to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91652 and leave this issue only for any still-reproducible ingress latency after v2026.6.11.

options.title: Close After Explicit Maintainer Decision
options.body: A maintainer can close this if they accept the shipped ingress-drain fix as sufficient and do not want a separate direct-message abort fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep As Umbrella Until Live Repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a live Telegram repro or maintainer trace confirms the exact remaining voice abort/fallback boundary, then split only after the root cause is known.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram release/current-main work and ownership signals make this the best available routing owner for deciding whether the shipped fix is sufficient or needs a follow-up.
